subject: System Design
title: Functional vs Non-Functional Requirements
description: A quick, practical guide to Functional vs Non-Functional Requirements.

hook.text: A chat app must send messages. That's functional. It must send them in under 100ms. That's non-functional.

buildup.text: Functional requirements define what the system does. Non-functional define how well it does it.

discovery.text: Latency, throughput, availability, and durability are the big four non-functional requirements.

twist.text: Teams often nail the functional requirements but ignore the non-functional ones until production breaks.

climax.text: Non-functional requirements are invisible until they fail — then they're the only thing anyone notices.

punchline.text: Users notice speed and uptime, not features.

quiz.question: What is a non-functional requirement?
options: How well the system performs, like latency and availability
